doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Mulligan's pipe, 'Donna Lee' and playing stoned
summary: The story of Gerry Mulligan passing him a pipe at a theater rehearsal and a solo he nearly missed.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: I have to ask you to tell the story that you told me years ago about when you and Mulligan were in Thornhill’s band and he introduced you to strong pot for the first time.
We were playing in a theater in some place in upper New York and we were rehearsing the line on “Donna Lee” which there was an arrangement of.

Yeah. He took his pipe out and passed it over and I said that I had tried it but I hadn’t really experienced it, so I took probably one “poke” and then we went down and at some point I had a sixteen bar solo on some tune and it was suddenly a very long distance to the microphone and I got there just in time, I might have been late actually. When I came back Gerry was hysterical, I remember that distinctly. I don’t know if anyone else was.
And you hadn’t played a note?

I don’t think so. [Laughs] or if I did it was probably a strange solo. In one other situation, I think that’s in the book, I actually did not play a note for thirty-two bars. I was stoned and I was just fascinated by the rhythm section with the guitar player, you know?
Yeah. It was a nice . . .”wow” I said, “look at that.” Finally, I took a bow just to do my “hammy” thing: That was one of my better solos.
[Laughs] I read somewhere that Gil and Barry Galbraith and Joe Schulman, and Billy Eckstine used to rent studio time at Nola’s and just get together and play time.
That’s all they did, just play time in the studio for their own pleasure.
They sounded like they enjoyed playing together.
